headline: Volume is building meaningfully and aerobic efficiency is improving — a strong foundation entering the second half of the year.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The 16% volume step-up over the last four weeks is real and well-distributed across multiple runs, not inflated by one outlier effort. What's more notable is that this increased volume is coming at lower average heart rate on comparable easy runs — suggesting your aerobic base is absorbing the load rather than being stressed by it. That combination of rising output and improving efficiency is the clearest positive signal in today's data.

The 20-week running streak reaching its all-time best is worth acknowledging not as a vanity metric, but as evidence of structural consistency — the kind that underpins both ultra durability and speed development. The recent back-to-back long efforts across consecutive days further reinforce that durability capacity is active and functioning.

One area worth keeping an eye on: strength frequency has dipped slightly relative to the prior block, and with running volume climbing, the balance between the two modalities deserves attention. Nothing alarming yet, but it's worth being deliberate about not letting strength work quietly compress as running load grows.
watch_items: Watch whether easy-run HR continues to trend down as volume holds or increases — this is the key aerobic efficiency signal to track over the next few weeks.
Monitor how strength session frequency responds to the elevated running block — a gradual squeeze is worth catching early.
The back-to-back long run pattern is valuable for ultra durability; notice how recovery quality holds if this structure repeats.
Sleep tracking is still sparse — as more nights accumulate, watch for any patterns between shorter sleep and next-day HR or perceived effort.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 145 km vs 125 km prior block (+16%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 146 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 7 vs 6 runs)
